, formerly known ?as IAC, withdrew its proposal to acquire MGM's remaining outstanding shares. People, which holds about 27% of MGM, offered $48.30 a share in cash in June, valuing the casino operator at more than $18 billion.

Diller said People had "decided not to pursue taking the company private at this time," as the deal's structure hadn't come together as hoped. He didn't close the door entirely, saying People remains interested in a possible strategic transaction with MGM and will consider alternatives. MGM's board said it's ready to continue as a standalone company.

That shifts the focus back to MGM's operations. The company owns properties covering roughly 40% of the Las Vegas Strip but has struggled with sluggish visitor traffic, leaning on its China assets, including Macau, and its digital business for growth in recent quarters. People began building its stake in 2020, when pandemic closures battered the shares.

title: MGM Stock Falls 9% as Diller Walks Away From Buyout
